items.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016
items.q: I will mention one specifically... There’s Lars Gullin. And he was a little bit famous even in the States... He really was a great composer. Fantastic musician

ctx.x: Any Swedish musicians that you particularly took note of?

Yes. I will mention one specifically. Of course there are many. There’s Lars Gullin. And he was a little bit famous even in the States. He was on the Down Beat list. And what he did, in the 50s and 60s, he was influenced by the Nordic classical music. And maybe © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

that’s not so very unique, especially later. But what he wrote songs inspired by that music but he made it into genuine jazz. Songs that were nice to play on, nice to improvise on. He really was a great composer. Fantastic musician, with a tragic life I’m sorry to say, but some great songs he wrote. At least in his early days he was a very melodic saxophone player like Stan Getz — not really — but very melodic and very beautiful.
